name: St. Andrew
bio:
Andrew was a fisherman from Bethsaida in Galilee and the brother of Simon Peter. He was first a disciple of John the Baptist, who pointed him to Jesus as the Lamb of God. Andrew immediately followed Christ and then brought his brother Peter to him, becoming the first-called of the apostles.

According to tradition, Andrew preached the Gospel in Greece and Asia Minor and was martyred at Patras on an X-shaped cross, which came to be known as Saint Andrew's Cross. He is venerated as the patron saint of Scotland, Russia, and Greece.

As a fisherman by trade, Andrew is invoked as the patron saint of fishermen and all who work at sea.
